Web design in Laredo, TX has a customer most towns never think about: the business on the other end of a shipment. A freight forwarder's next client might be an importer in Ohio or a manufacturer in Monterrey, looking at three Laredo firms on a laptop and calling the one that answers the obvious questions first. Maurice Johnson, a Texan who writes every page by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas, builds sites that do that, and you see a free demo before you pay.

A border city whose main street is a bridge

The Laredo Economic Development Corporation describes the Port of Laredo as the busiest of all U.S. border crossings and third among more than 450 airports, seaports and border crossings nationwide. Port Laredo handled $353.94 billion in trade in 2025, and more than 97% of it was tied to Mexico. Trucks cross at the World Trade Bridge and the Colombia Solidarity Bridge, and Mines Road (FM 1472), which links the two, is lined with industrial parks and warehouses.

That traffic supports a long list of small firms: customs brokers, freight forwarders, carriers, cross-dock and warehouse operators, truck and trailer repair, and the restaurants, tire shops and services that drivers use. The Laredo Chamber of Commerce, founded in 1915, counts transportation and logistics companies among more than 700 members.

What a Laredo logistics website should show first

  1. What you handleCustoms entries, forwarding, transloading, dry van, flatbed, refrigerated, storage. Name the services in the words a shipping manager searches for, not just a slogan.
  2. Where and whenWhich crossings you work, your yard or warehouse location, your office hours and whether someone can be reached after hours when a load is stuck.
  3. Who will answerThe languages your staff speaks, a direct phone number and an email that goes to a person who can quote.
  4. How to get a rateA short quote form that asks for origin, destination, commodity and timing, and sends it straight to your inbox.
  5. Why a shipper can trust youYour real licenses, authority and insurance details, stated plainly. No stock claims.

Web design for the Laredo businesses that serve the drivers

Not every Laredo company works the trade directly. The electrician who keeps a warehouse's dock doors and lights running, the diesel shop, the taqueria that opens before the morning crossing rush: each needs a simpler site. Hours, location, what you fix or serve, and a phone number that dials with one tap. Google ranks local results on relevance, distance and prominence, so a page that says clearly where you are, and which side of town or which corridor you serve, helps the driver who is searching from the cab two miles away.

For most of these owners, Starter at $497 is enough: five hand-written pages, a contact form that emails every lead, Google Maps and hours, live in 7 to 14 days, and you own it. A broker or carrier that wants pages for each service and each lane it runs may need Pro at $997 or Agency at $1,997. We do not sell page counts; a few clear pages beat a stack of thin ones.

Free business help in Laredo

The Small Business Development Center at Texas A&M International University offers free, confidential one-on-one advising on financing, business planning and marketing, plus training and free webinars. It serves the tri-county area of Webb, Jim Hogg and Zapata counties. The Laredo Chamber of Commerce is the city's oldest business group and a good place to meet the firms you work alongside.

Remote, from the other side of Texas

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Laredo. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

That suits a trade town used to doing business with people it has never met in person: a call, an email, a shared link.

Tell us your company name, what you move or fix, and which crossing you work. The preview is free.

Common questions

How much does web design cost for a Laredo business?

With us it is a printed, one-time price: Starter is $497 for five pages, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997. After launch, hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent. Other designers may bill hourly or monthly, so ask anyone you talk to for the full first-year cost in writing.

Should a Laredo customs broker or freight company list the languages it works in?

Yes. Many of your callers will be shippers, importers and carriers on both sides of the border, and knowing they can be helped in English or Spanish before they call saves everyone time. Say which languages your staff speaks right on the contact page. If you want the site itself in more than one language, raise it when you ask for the demo and Maurice will tell you honestly what your package can cover.

Is web design in Laredo different for a trucking company than for a restaurant?

Very. A restaurant's customer wants the menu, the hours and directions. A carrier's or broker's customer is another business that wants to know your lanes, your equipment, your authority and insurance details, and how to request a rate. The pages, the order of information and the forms are built differently for each.

Can I see a Laredo website before I pay for it?

Yes. Send your business name and what you do through the free demo page, and Maurice builds a preview for your company. If it is not right, you owe nothing.
